overview_markdown:
Ouroboros is a self-modifying AI agent implemented in Python that autonomously writes and rewrites its own code, maintaining a persistent identity and background consciousness across restarts. Unlike a typical coding assistant, it operates as a native desktop application for macOS, Linux, and Windows with a web UI, local model support, and a layered safety system combining a hardcoded sandbox with policy-based LLM safety checks.

Architecturally, Ouroboros emphasizes autonomous evolution: it includes a constitution, reusable live cards for background tasks, and an idempotent scratch workspace for safe file operations. Recent commits show robust engineering for benchmark harnesses (GAIA, SWE-Pro) with bwrap filesystem isolation to prevent answer leakage, cost hard-stop budgets, and protected-artifact policies. A companion skills marketplace, OuroborosHub, allows community distribution of transport bridges and tools.

Compared to OpenClaw—a personal AI assistant focused on multi-channel communication and ease of use—Ouroboros leans into self-evolution and local-first desktop autonomy. It lacks OpenClaw’s broad chat-platform integrations and enterprise multi-user story, but offers stronger experimental isolation for agent safety and a unique self-improving codebase.
